verdict: McKesson moved $111B of medicines through its warehouses in one quarter and kept $1.2B — profit rose 10% as oncology distribution grew 24% and buybacks lifted EPS 17%.

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: distribution economics: a thin slice of a huge flow

segments.name: North American Pharmaceutical
segments.note: Distributing prescription drugs to pharmacies, hospitals and clinics across North America — one of the largest drug wholesaling operations in the world.

segments.name: Oncology & Multispecialty
segments.note: Supplying cancer and specialty clinics with high-value drugs and related services — the fastest-growing part of McKesson.

segments.name: Medical-Surgical Solutions
segments.note: Surgical and medical supplies for doctor offices and other care sites. McKesson plans to spin this segment off as its own company.

segments.name: Prescription Technology Solutions
segments.note: Software and services that help patients get approved for, afford and stay on specialty medicines.

opex.name: Selling, distribution, general & administrative
opex.note: Warehouses, delivery fleets, sales and back office for moving $111B of product.

opex.name: Restructuring & impairment, net
opex.note: $85M of restructuring, impairment and related charges, less a $2M net credit on claims and litigation.

otherDetail: Other income of $63M, less $105M of interest expense.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding. McKesson keeps about $1.10 of every $100 it handles.

takeaways.title: Oncology is the growth engine
takeaways.text: Oncology & Multispecialty revenue jumped 24% to $15.0B on demand for cancer drugs, while the core North American Pharmaceutical business grew 6% to $91.4B.

takeaways.title: Buybacks amplify profit growth
takeaways.text: Net income attributable to McKesson rose 10%, but EPS rose 17% — the diluted share count fell 6% year over year as buybacks shrank the denominator.

takeaways.title: A thin slice of a giant flow
takeaways.text: Drug distribution runs on razor-thin margins: $107.0B of every $111.0B went straight to buying the medicines, leaving a 3.6% gross margin to run the network and earn from.

footerNote: Net income of $1,218M is the amount attributable to McKesson; consolidated net income was $1,296M, of which $78M belonged to noncontrolling interests.
